phases.title: Commit the already-applied prod reference-seed fix + wrapper script

outputs.notes: Ops-verification commit only, no schema change. Verified all three files matched the plan's expected content exactly: scripts/seed-reference-data.ts jsonPath now points at docs/archive/compliance-research/homeschool-requirements-2026-06-27.json (fixed from the missing docs/compliance-research/... path); scripts/seed-reference-prod.ts mirrors scripts/migrate-prod.ts (loads DATABASE_URL_PROD, remaps to DATABASE_URL, execSync's seed-reference-data.ts via npx tsx); package.json's db:seed:reference:prod entry (dotenv -e .env.local -- tsx scripts/seed-reference-prod.ts) was already present in the committed baseline (package.json's only working-tree diff was the routine pre-commit version bump). Reference seed already run and verified against prod 2026-07-16: 66 compliance_rulesets across 7 states (TX/FL/NY/PA/CA/MI/CT), 8 starter badge_definitions — read-only verification, no schema change here. Committed as 4b48c33. IMPORTANT for next worker/orchestrator: `npm run build` fails in this sandbox at static generation of /(shell)/about/page — it calls listChangelogEntries() which needs a live DB connection; TCP connects to the Render Postgres host but the Postgres protocol handshake hangs indefinitely (confirmed via direct postgres.js and raw TCP probes), causing Next's 60s-per-attempt static-export timeout after 3 retries. Confirmed via `git stash` that this reproduces identically with this phase's 3 files stashed out — it is a pre-existing sandbox network/DB-connectivity limitation, NOT caused by this phase's changes, and outside this phase's file scope (features/lib/server/db.ts, app/(shell)/about/page.tsx). npm test passes fully (239 suites, 2110 tests) since tests mock the repository boundary. Later phases whose doneWhen includes `npm run build` should expect this same failure mode in this environment and should not attribute it to their own changes without first checking build fails identically on a clean stash.

phases.title: G1 — Persist Planning Defaults & Records/Compliance settings tabs with an explicit Save button

outputs.notes: Route pattern followed: features/badges/api/router.ts + features/badges/api/routes/settings.ts (most recently added sibling router) — new top-level GET/PUT /api/settings route added to app/api/[...slug]/route.ts's handleRoute() dispatch (new 'settings' slug case, after 'badges'). Reused the existing features/settings/server/repository.ts (getAllHouseholdSettings/setHouseholdSetting against household_settings) unchanged — no duplication. Exact setting keys used: planning.maxLessonsPerDay (number), planning.carryForward ('none'|'next-day'|'next-week'), records.trackingMethod ('days'|'hours'), records.exportFormat ('pdf'|'csv'). Front contract for G7/G8: features/settings/front/services/api.ts exports settingsApi.getSettings() -> ApiResponse<Record<string,unknown>> and settingsApi.updateSettings(patch: Record<string,unknown>) -> ApiResponse<Record<string,unknown>|null> (PUT merges/upserts only the provided keys, returns the full updated map). Both PlanningDefaultsTab.tsx and RecordsComplianceTab.tsx load on mount, track dirty state against last-saved values, and disable the 'Save changes' button until dirty — confirmed via integration tests. No auto-save on change, per plan decision. Found and fixed a test race during TDD: an integration test's initial waitFor assertion (toHaveValue matching the default state, which happened to equal the mocked loaded value) passed before the component's load effect actually finished, so a subsequent userEvent.selectOptions fired on a still-disabled <select> and silently no-op'd. Fixed by asserting `.not.toBeDisabled()` in the waitFor instead of relying on the value coincidentally matching. `npm run build` fails identically to the phase-0 note (static generation of /(shell)/about times out on a DB handshake) — confirmed via `git stash`/`git stash pop` with this phase's files fully stashed out: same 3-retry 60s timeout on /(shell)/about, unrelated to any file in this phase's scope. `npx tsc --noEmit` shows only pre-existing unrelated errors (subjects/messaging/feedback-steward fixtures) — nothing in features/settings/**.
